scope: Read-only latency diagnosis for the rhythm tester on the current WHP01K Bluetooth output. No microphone capture, unrelated audio capture, system default changes, or existing-app shutdown.

environment.requested_qt_format: 48 kHz, stereo, PCM16; QAudioDevice.isFormatSupported returned true
environment.qt_warning: No sample format supported found for device bluez_output.C4_6E_7B_12_03_2E.1, although the requested PCM16 format reports supported and the sink processed samples.

qt_qiodevice_ring_buffer.interpretation: The Qt QIODevice ring buffer was full at the sampled active times. This is an app/backend queue capacity observation; it does not by itself establish the exact additional acoustic delay because processedUSecs has no documented audible-presentation guarantee.

pipewire_sink_latency.direction: Input latency parameter on the Audio/Sink node
pipewire_sink_latency.process_latency_parameter: No ProcessLatency parameter was reported for this node.
pipewire_sink_latency.interpretation: PipeWire reports 150 ms downstream playback latency for the WHP01K sink. This is a graph-reported estimate/latency parameter, not an acoustic loopback measurement at the ear.

qt_clock_probe.interpretation: In this approximately 2-second sample, processedUSecs stopped during suspend and then advanced at approximately the active playback rate; no evidence of sustained drift was observed. The sample is too short to quantify long-term clock drift, and it cannot show when sound reached the listener.

transport_restart_behavior.current_implementation: AudioTransport._discard_backend calls QAudioSink.stop() for seek, click-mix rebuild, reload, and stop.
transport_restart_behavior.qt_documented_stop_behavior: On Linux and Darwin, QAudioSink.stop synchronously drains the underlying audio buffer; QAudioSink.reset immediately halts and discards buffered audio.
transport_restart_behavior.risk: Seek or set_clicks can spend time draining old queued audio before starting the new sink, while the application rebases the logical position to the target/current processed frame. The user may hear old queued samples or an apparent gap around a restart. This is a code-path risk, not proven as the cause of the reported mismatch.

conclusions: Qt documents processedUSecs only as audio data processed since start(); it does not document this clock as sound already audible at the listener.

The current WHP01K path has a measured graph-reported sink latency of 150 ms, and Qt's actual QIODevice ring buffer is 250 ms. These are distinct queue/latency observations and must not be blindly added as a precise end-to-end delay.
The observed processed counter follows active playback and pauses across suspend; no obvious long-term drift was found in the short probe.
A true acoustic output-delay value remains uncalibrated. The PipeWire estimate cannot account exactly for Bluetooth endpoint buffering, DSP, codec, or the listener-side presentation time.
recommendations: Add a separate output-presentation compensation value used to align visual playhead, on-screen hit windows/effects, and audible audio. Keep this distinct from player input correction; the latter needs its own measurement and should not inherit output latency automatically.

For the tester, expose the selected output device and report preferred/actual format and graph latency. WHP01K currently has Unknown preferred format despite accepting requested PCM16; a selectable wired/USB output is a useful low-latency comparison without changing the OS default.

Optionally test a smaller QIODevice ring-buffer target (for example 20–50 ms) and measure underruns and PipeWire-reported latency again. A smaller Qt ring can reduce one source of queued audio, but it will not remove Bluetooth sink latency and may increase dropouts.

Consider QAudioSink.reset() for interactive seek/click-rebuild teardown to discard queued old audio immediately; retain stop/drain where natural completion requires graceful drain. Validate behavior on the target Qt/backend before changing code.

estimated total output latency includes sink, buffer, and transport

limitations: No microphone or loopback capture was performed, so acoustic arrival time was not measured.
PipeWire reports a fixed 150 ms sink latency, but endpoint Bluetooth buffering may vary and is not directly measured here.
The Qt clock comparison lasted about two seconds; it is not a long-term drift study.
The QIODevice ring capacity was full during the sampled instants, but its exact additive contribution to end-to-end audible latency is not inferable from these observations alone.
